title: GraphQL error response that echoes a supplied secret, or elides it
summary: A synthetic transcript of a GraphQL request whose variables map holds a secret, followed by an error response that either repeats the value inside the message string, or reports only the variable name and leaves the value out.
rationale: The specification gives the response error message and extensions member no content rules, and leaves it to the implementer what an error reveals. The value in a response is the same bytes as the value in the request: repeating it inside a message string, where its quotation marks are JSON-escaped, is a second occurrence with its own span, and a reader that only inspects the request, or only the first occurrence, leaves one copy exposed. A response that names the variable and omits the value has no second span. The echo text itself is an invented illustration, not a documented behaviour of any server; nothing here says that servers echo supplied values.

expectation.rationale: Flagged: every occurrence of the documented-shape key is a span, the request occurrence and, in the echo fixture, the message occurrence. A transcript with an elided response has one span, in the request. The key shape is the family contract; the specifications say only that error messages are intended for developers and are otherwise free-form, so the claim that a repeated copy of the same key is the same credential rests on the family, not on the GraphQL text. Project-authored, not independent.

sources.supports: Every error contains a message string intended for the developer; an error may carry an extensions entry whose map has no additional restrictions on its contents.
A response may contain an extensions entry reserved for implementers, with no additional restrictions on its contents.

Implementers are expected to limit information revealed via errors and to log requests safely without revealing sensitive information; these are stated as expectations of the implementer, outside the specification.
The quotation mark must be escaped inside a JSON string.
The key is documented as always 69 characters; the alphabet and segment split are tool-corroborated, not this citation.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. Authored from the cited pages read on 2026-10-04, before any scanner was consulted. Research for #197 (parent #158). Origin of the inputs: evidence-derived and synthetic, not observed in a real incident or product; the request shapes follow the specification examples and the response texts are invented. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Partial and masked echoes are covered by the existing cases bare-prefixes-and-truncated-tokens and already-masked-values and are projected in the fixture set against them, not restated here. Whether a product masks response text and the exact range it covers stay downstream.
